name: Apollo 14
short_status: Third crewed Moon landing. Antares set down 5 Feb 1971 at Fra Mauro (Apollo 13's lost target). Shepard and Mitchell logged 9h23m of EVA; returned 9 Feb 1971. Success.
tagline: NASA · United States · Crewed landing · 1971 · The space race Success
stats: total time spacewalking on the surface
short of Cone Crater's rim when they turned back
Shepard's age, oldest moonwalker at the time

facts.label: Crew
facts.value: Alan B. Shepard Jr. (commander), Stuart A. Roosa (command module pilot, stayed in orbit), Edgar D. Mitchell (lunar module pilot)

facts.label: Launch
facts.value: 31 Jan 1971, 4:03:02 p.m. EST (21:03 UTC), Kennedy Space Center LC-39A; delayed 40 minutes by rain showers, reportedly the first US crewed launch held by weather

facts.label: Docking trouble
facts.value: Six attempts were needed before Kitty Hawk achieved a hard dock with Antares after transposition; no cause for the balky latches was ever found in flight

facts.label: Abort-switch fault
facts.value: A floating solder ball intermittently closed the LM abort switch, risking a false abort during descent; MIT engineers devised a software patch, radioed up and keyed in, to make the computer ignore the signal

facts.label: Lunar touchdown
facts.value: 5 Feb 1971, 09:18:11 UTC, Fra Mauro formation; the most accurate landing of the six crewed Apollo touchdowns relative to its target

facts.label: Surface EVAs
facts.value: Two moonwalks: EVA-1 about 4 h 48 min, EVA-2 about 4 h 35 min, total about 9 h 23 min

facts.label: Cone Crater climb
facts.value: On EVA-2 the crew pulled a two-wheeled cart (the MET) toward Cone Crater but turned back roughly 20 to 30 m short of the rim without realizing how close they were

facts.label: Golf and "javelin"
facts.value: Shepard hit two golf balls with a club head on a sample-tool handle; per a 2021 image analysis the balls went about 24 and 40 yards. Mitchell threw a lunar scoop handle like a javelin

facts.label: Surface stay
facts.value: About 33.5 hours on the Moon (touchdown 5 Feb 09:18 UTC to liftoff 6 Feb 18:48 UTC)

facts.label: Samples returned
facts.value: About 42.8 kg (94 lb) of rock and soil, a record at the time

facts.label: Splashdown
facts.value: 9 Feb 1971, 21:05 UTC (4:05 p.m. EST), South Pacific; recovered by USS New Orleans

timeline: Launch, delayed 40 minutes by rain showers, 21:03 UTC
Six docking attempts before a hard dock with Antares
Abort-switch software patch radioed up before powered descent

EVA-1: ALSEP deployed, Shepard becomes fifth human to walk on the Moon
EVA-2: Cone Crater climb; crew turns back short of the rim
Shepard hits two golf balls before Antares lifts off, 18:48:42 UTC
Splashdown in the South Pacific, recovered by USS New Orleans, 21:05 UTC
